name: demo
title: Communication-content ladder — demo campaign
subtitle: 3 conditions × 2 tasks × 2 seeds · 6 min per arm · 4 concurrent
description:
# Goal
Does the *content* of what agents share change where a team ends up, or only how fast it gets there?

# Design
Three communication conditions (none / prose lessons / verbatim code) on two optimisation tasks, two seeds each. Every arm is a team of 5 agents with a fixed wall-clock budget; the metric is the best latency the team verifies before the budget runs out.

# Pre-registration
- Claims are made only at the pooled level (both tasks together).
- Primary test: lessons > none, paired over (task, seed), Wilcoxon, effect ≥ 0.05 in frontier-ratio.
- Small n is direction only: n=2 per cell tells us where to spend the next round, not what is true.

# Budget
12 arms × 6 min ≈ 25 min wall-clock at 4 concurrent, then ~30 min of analysis.

plots.title: Best-so-far latency vs wall-clock
plots.explain: Median over seeds of each team's best verified latency; band = IQR (≥3 seeds). Dashed = baseline final median. Lower is better.

plots.title: Best-so-far latency vs # evaluations
plots.explain: Same curves on an evaluation-count axis: separates 'smarter per eval' from 'more evals per minute'.

plots.title: Best-so-far latency vs cumulative tokens
plots.explain: Token-efficiency view (H3). A curve that sits left of another reached the same quality for fewer tokens.

plots.title: Final latency by condition
plots.explain: Bar = median over seeds, whisker = min–max, dots = arms. Provisional (best-so-far) for unfinished arms.

plots.title: Cost vs final latency
plots.explain: One dot per arm. Bottom-left is the frontier: cheaper and faster.

plots.title: Time to reach the baseline endpoint
plots.explain: Fraction of arms that have reached the baseline's final median by minute x. Arms that never do stay below 1.

plots.title: Median final latency, normalised to row best
plots.explain: 1.00 = best condition for that task; 1.20 = 20% slower than the best.

plots.title: Evaluations per arm
plots.explain: Does communication change how much agents evaluate, not just what they find?
